contract:
# Balanced release candidate lifecycle

Outcome: retain and pair the existing thread-local live release-candidate proof through object publication and raw/PHP cloning; reuse that existing proof at direct owner retirement. This is general ownership metadata, with no workload recognizer or altered PHP release ordering.

Baseline: clean c6ac2dfa, runtime SHA f1ebb4d1a2249bf68f6a2e648c67f3781f286948f133d52587990be7d9708e8e; accepted named-types PGO 73.4727G versus PHP 10.3379G. Early baseline is the exact test-fast named-types exploratory executable, SHA d298eda3ea7118e72c3d5269822803510e2600171331376ae6df30cd5d223c4a.

Evidence: preceding exact phase profile attributes 3.5383G inclusive to retire_owned_frame_value, including 997.96M direct preparation and 977.09M array preparation (nested costs overlap). Objects get OBJECT_VM_RELEASE_TRACKED at declared construction or explicit native tracking; Value::object retains only the deep checkpoint, and deferred_object clears all lifecycle flags. PhpObject::drop untracks only if that lost bit survives. Thus registration and destruction are not paired; one prior candidate can permanently hold the global release gate open. Derived raw PhpObject cloning also copies a tracked bit without its matching increment.

Hypothesis: balancing metadata makes the existing false global verdict usable after the final candidate dies. A direct release cannot need a PHP callback when the exact existing global proof and weak/lazy/fiber guards rule all such work out. Preserve object storage finalization/stack growth, callbacks, exceptions, construction suppression, resurrection, generator/native/resource and weak/lazy/fiber semantics. The global proof remains conservative while a retired-but-live destructor object survives. Unknown dynamic objects use the existing explicit tracking protocol.

Ownership: sole integrating task, isolated codex/perf-phpstan-cold checkout, value/mod.rs, call_frames.rs and focused tests. No unsafe or ABI expansion; canonical direct/tree planner unchanged whenever work remains possible.

Gates: focused exact live-count tests covering publication, raw/PHP clones, deferred publication and return to initial count; release-gate/owner/destructor/generator/weak/resource/deep correctness if the early filter succeeds. Native phase output must match both baseline and PHP. Early test-fast >=0.5% instruction saving before fresh PGO, broad relevant features or controls. Accepted release requires independent fresh PGO improvement, focused feature checks, independent controls, RSS, code size, fmt, unsafe inventory and cleanup. Preserve all evidence and known PHP gaps as failures.

Stop rule: reject callback loss, count imbalance, source drift, any changed exact output, or early native saving below 0.5%. Keep an independently verified correctness repair only if removing an unsafe false-negative count is established; an unaccepted performance gate stays explicit. Native architecture evidence is x86-64 only.

Review: the early direct guard grows instructions 0.0964% in two alternating native pairs, and is removed in full. The counter lifecycle imbalance remains a demonstrated independent correctness defect; keep evaluating only balanced publication/cloning, without new runtime planner guards or a performance claim. Verify focused release, weak, generator, resource, deep and feature semantics and exact application output; quantify the final metadata-only variant separately.

Three injected regression cases fail on original runtime as expected and are not counted as passes.
native_scope: x86-64 only; no architecture-specific source, lowering or ABI change; ARM64 execution not measured
performance_scope: No instruction or timing saving claimed. Two alternating PGO phase pairs and five independent control pairs; exact full PHP output and fresh TMPDIR. Four control instruction medians increase at most 0.01593%; control time medians at most 0.724%. Whole-command RSS check is one sample per runtime, not phase instruction evidence.
infrastructure_failures: The initial regression-proof copy lacked four compile-time test/data inputs and failed compilation. After supplying those files, all three original-runtime assertions failed as expected. The failed compile is retained separately.
